ORAL JUDGMENT (PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE MAULIK J.SHELAT)
1.

The present appeal has been filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act (the MV Act) challenging judgment and award dated 06.05.2011 passed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (Auxilliary), Surendranagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition (MACP) No.120 of 2000.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition (MACP) No.120 of 2000
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The parties will be referred as per their original position in the Claim Petition.

2. Short facts:
2.1 On 11.07.1999 deceased Tusharbhai was pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No. GJ 13 D 9147 owned by opponent No.7 which was driven by opponent No.8.

They were proceeded towards Chotila, at that time, one tanker bearing registration No.MH 04 P 1437, motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ 03 F 8283 and one another tanker No. GJ 2 V 4899 came from Chotila side.

They appears to be collision between all four vehicles wherein pillion rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ 13 D 9147 i.e. Tusharbhai had sustained serious injuries and died during course of his treatment on 24.11.1999.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 2.2

The death of Tusharbhai was arising out of use of motor vehicles involved in the accident, his legal heirs have chosen to file MACP No.120 of 2000 under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- to be recovered from driver, owner and insurance company of vehicles involved in the accident.
Notice came to be served upon the opponents of claim petition wherein driver and owner of the respective vehicles have chosen not to appear.
Thereby, not contested the claim petition.
Whereas respondent Nos. 2, 4 and 6 insurance company of different vehicles involved in the accident have appeared and filed their respective written statement at Exh.13, 18 and 27 respectively.
The claimants have tendered their oral and documentary evidence in support of their claim.
There is no counter evidence submitted by any of the opponents.

2.3 Documentary evidence produced by the claimants are as under:

After hearing the parties and appreciating evidence on record, the tribunal has found driver of tanker No. MH 04 P 1437, 30% negligent, driver of tanker No.4899 negligent to the extent of 20% whereas rider of both the motorcycles found 5% each negligent respectively.
The deceased was pillion rider of motorcycle No. GJ 13 D 9147.
It was the case of composite negligence whereby claimants can recover entire compensation from any of the tortfeasors.
So the tribunal has held all the opponents jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, after appreciating evidence and the arguments made by learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/12/2024 undefined advocate for the respective parties, in all, tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.8,24,800/- with 9% interest from the date of petition till its realization in favour of claimants which was to be paid by all the opponents jointly and severally.

2.5 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with not granting adequate compensation in favour of the claimants they have challenged impugned judgment and award by way of present appeal except claimant No.1, remaining claimants are in appeal.
Original claimant No.5 happens to be father of the deceased was joined as respondent No.9 in the present appeal who reported died.
It appears from reading of oral evidence of claimants No.3 - widow of deceased Tusharbhai that her father in law i.e. claimant No.1 already died during pendency of claim petition.
It further appears that legal heirs of deceased claimant No.1 were not brought on record as except claimant No.2 and children of deceased Tusharbhai other legal heirs were not brought on record.

Tribunal has granted 25% of total compensation in favour of original claimant No.1 who already NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/12/2024 undefined died during pendency of the claim petition.

We would have observed something about the procedure undertaken by the tribunal while granting award in favour of the dead person but considering the fact that impugned judgment and award is of the year 2011 and also keeping in mind benevolent provision of law, this Court would not like to become too technical but just to advance justice to the claimants, we have decided to hear the matter on its own merits without insisting for rectification of impugned judgment and award.
However, this order may not be consider as precedent in any other matter.
4. Submissions of the appellant - claimants 4.1

Learned advocate appearing for the original claimants would submit that deceased was owing a shop of electronic NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined items and it is registered in the name of Shri Shakti Electronics and he was aged about 30 years old at the time of accident, the income considered by the tribunal of the deceased is much on lower side, requires to be reconsidered.

She would submit that the tribunal has considered only Rs.3000/- income per month as income of deceased by observing that there is no supporting documentary evidence submitted by the claimants to substantiate their claim with regard to income of deceased which is erroneous.

She would further submit that it has remained undisputed before the tribunal that deceased was running electronic shop and doing its repair in City of Surendranagar as the claimants have produced registration certificate of shop in favour of deceased by local Nagarpalika under Bombay Establishment of Shops Act, 1948 (Exh.87).

She would further submit that deceased was having technical education having certificate issued by Mashar and Company (Exh.88) would prove that deceased was skilled person having knowledge of repairing of electronic items.

She would thus submit that at least Rs.7000/- per NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/12/2024 undefined month income of deceased ought to have been considered by the tribunal.

4.2 She would further submit that there were in all five dependent claimants then as per the decision in case of Sarla Varma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. reported in 2009 (6) SCC 121,

She would further submit that as per the decision in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. reported in 2017 (13) Scale 12, 40% future prospective rise of income should be considered as deceased was aged about 30 years old.

sentences.text: She would further submit that considering the age of the deceased as 30 years, appropriate multiplier would be 17 instead of 18.

4.3 She would also submit that deceased died during the course of treatment which took almost three and half months than adequate amount under the head of pain, shock and suffering is required to be granted, as tribunal has granted NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined only Rs.15,000/-, which according to her ought to have been granted Rs. 2,50,000/.

4.4 She would further submit that two attendants were required during the course of treatment which is confirmed from the certificate issued by Gokul Hospital and Trauma Centre (Exh.75), so adequate amount towards attendant charges for such treatment requires to be granted.

It is also submitted that during the course of treatment, deceased had undertaken series of hospitalization,
amount towards transportation, special diet etc. requires to be granted higher then what has been Tusharbhai Manharlal Since Decd. ...

5. Submissions of the Respondents:
5.1
Per contra, learned advocates for the insurance company would submit that there is no error committed by the tribunal while granting compensation in favour of the claimants.

They would submit that considering the facts and circumstances and year in which accident took place the tribunal has decided just and reasonable income of the deceased in absence of any proof of income.
They would submit that claimants could have submitted sales and purchase receipts of the deceased if he was in the business of the selling and repairing of electronic items.
They would further submit that claimants could have submitted account books of deceased to substantiate claim of income alleged in their claim petition and oral evidence.

They have drawn attention of this Court that in her oral evidence, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined claimant No.3 - widow of the deceased has categorically stated that after deducting expenses of business, deceased was used to earn Net Annual Income of Rs.40,000/-.
5.2 They would submit that against claim of Rs.40,000/- per year, tribunal has already considered Rs.36,000/- per year which may not be disturbed.

Nonetheless, in view of the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), Magma General Insurance (supra) and Satinder Kaur (supra), they have fairly conceded that an appropriate future rise of income as well as conventional amount may be granted in favour of the claimants.

5.3 Further, they would submit that nothing has been produced by the claimants to substantiate higher attendant charges, so also not submitted actual transport expenses during the course of treatment which might have been taken in Rajkot City.

So, they would submit that amount which has been awarded by the tribunal under the other heads is just and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined reasonable, no interference is required by this Court.
5.4 In view of above, they have requested this Court to pass appropriate order in accordance with law.

sentences.text: Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and perused the record and proceedings of the case.
No other and further arguments are made.
7. Point of Determination.
7.1 Whether in the facts and circumstances of the case, any error committed by Tribunal while awarding compensation?
7.2 Whether amount of filial consortium to be granted in favour of claimant no.1 - father of deceased who died during pendency of the claim petition?

8. Findings of the Court;
8.1

We have examined the claim of claimants in detail and also analyzed submissions made by respondent advanced in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined light of the evidence on record.

As there are multiple grounds which are raised by the appellants during the course of arguments under which claimants are claiming additional compensation, this Court would like to deal each separately.

8.2 Consideration of income of deceased:
8.2.1
The deceased was aged about 30 years old at the time of accident running shop in the city of Surendranagar
. He would having certificate of registration of his shop issued by local self government being Bombay Shops and Establishment Act.

He was also possessing certificate of Meshar and company certifying that deceased had successfully completed the course of VCR Technician and these factors if taking into account and keeping in mind year of accident i.e. 1999, we would not find any exaggeration in claimants claim regarding income of the deceased Rs.40,000/- per annum in their oral evidence submitted through widow of deceased i.e. claimant No.3. 8.2.2

When the claimants themselves contended before the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined tribunal that deceased was used to earn Rs. 40,000/ per year (net income) than now, it would not be appropriate on the part of the ld.
Advocate
for the claimants to submit and to consider higher income of the deceased i.e. Rs. 7000/ p.m. -
Rs. 84,000/ per year than contended before the tribunal

. Moreover, there is neither any accounts of business of the deceased produced on record nor any ITRs of the deceased on record justifying such higher claim and even no person working with the deceased was examined.
So, keeping all these factors into account and year of the accident i.e. 1999, we are not inclined to consider the income of deceased @ Rs. 84,000/ per year.
8.2.3 Thus, considering the aforesaid aspect of the case and no rebuttal evidence lead by opponent - insurance company, we are inclined to accept the version of claimants.
Thereby, accepting deceased was used to earn Rs.40,000/- per annum.
Hence, we are assessing and fixing the income of deceased to Rs.40,000/- per year.

Future Prospective Income 8.3.1
The tribunal has not at all awarded any future prospective rise of income of deceased while granting loss of dependency to the claimants.

It is well settled position of law in view of decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra) in a case of self employed also, Court/ tribunal has to consider the future prospective income of the deceased /
victim.

As deceased was aged about 30 years also being self employed at the time of accident, 40%
future prospective income requires to be considered.
Accordingly, there would be an addition of Rs.16,000/- as future prospective income of the deceased.
8.4 Personal deduction of deceased:
8.4.1 The deceased was survived by his widow, parents and two minor children at the time of accident.
The claimant NO.1- father of deceased was earning from his service may not considered as his dependent.
Nonetheless, there are other 4 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined dependents / claimants.
As per the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court Sarla Verma (supra) though there are 4 dependents / claimants on deceased, 1/4th personal expenses is required to be deducted instead of 1/3rd.
8.5 Conventional amount 8.5.1

As per the recent passed decision of Honourable Supreme Court in case of Rojalini Nayak & Ors. vs. Ajit Sahoo & Ors reported in 2024 (8) SCC 239 and also other decisions of Honourable Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra),
Magma General Insurance (supra) and Satinder Kaur (supra) , each claimant would entitle to receive consortium of Rs.48,400/-.

entities.text: Rojalini Nayak & Ors. vs. Ajit Sahoo & Ors reported in 2024 (8) SCC 239
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8.5.2 At this stage, we would like to observe that claimant No.1 - father of deceased already died during the course of trial before the tribunal and having so observed herein above, his legal heirs were not even brought on record.
So, we are not granting loss of filial consortium to claimant No.1 who NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined already died.

Even otherwise an amount of filial consortium is the personal claim of an individual which r e q u i r e s t o b e a w a r d e d t o a n i n d i v i d u a l a s p e r s o n c o n c e r n l o s s company/companionship of deceased.

As per Section 306 of Indian Succession Act,
such personal claim would not survive after death of a person in favour of his surviving legal heirs.
Thus, in view of aforesaid fact and provision of law, we are not inclined to grant any filial consortium to claimant no.1- father of deceased who died during pendency of the claim petition.
8.5.3 In view of above, we are inclined to grant Rs.48,400/- to each claimant except claimant No.1.
8.6 Loss of estate and future expenses 8.6.1
The claimants would get Rs.18,150/- each as per the aforesaid decision of the Honourable Apex Court for loss to estate and funeral expenses.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 8.7

Pain,
shock and suffering 8.7.1
It has come on record that deceased was survived after accident which took place on 11.07.1999 and died during the course of medical treatment on 24.11.1999.
He would for about three and half months must have undergone pain and suffering of accidental injuries which he had received due to the accident.

It remained undisputed before the tribunal that cause of death was due to injuries sustained by him, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case of the present case and considering nature of injuries sustained by the claimants, who of-course conscious during the course of treatment, but having intermittently long hospitalization before his death, we are inclined to grant Rs.30,000/- towards pain, shock and suffering instead of Rs.15,000/- granted by the tribunal.
8.8 Attendant charges, special diet and transport 8.8.1

As per impugned certificate issued by Dr. Prakash Modha submitted at Exh.75 would suggest that deceased was required NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined two attendants during the course of his medical treatment from 11.07.1999 to 28.09.1999 and might have required for his subsequent treatment till he died.

So considering aforesaid medical evidence which remained undisputed before the tribunal, claimants would entitle to receive reasonable attendant charges in absence of any actual payment made to the attendant.

Keeping in mind the year of accident and minimum wages prevailing at the time of accident in State of Gujarat, which is around Rs.2000/- per month for any skilled person, so on guess work considering the period of hospitalization and till death of deceased, we would like to grant Rs.15000/- as attendant charges to the claimants instead of Rs.5000/- so granted by the tribunal.

8.8.2 So far as special diet and transport expenses is concerned except bare words of the claimants nothing has been brought on record by the claimants which can substantiate from claim made in their written arguments submitted before the tribunal at Exh.97.
So, according to us tribunal was justified in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined granting Rs.5000/- each toward special diet and transport charges.
8.9 Medical Expenses 8.9.1
So far as medical expenses are concerned sum of Rs.3,05,300/- was awarded by the tribunal to the claimants which was actual expenditure and supporting medical bills are produced on record at Exh.90.
There is no dispute raised by the claimants for granting any higher amount under such head.

9. Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion, findings and reasons which are assigned herein above,
tribunal has committed an error while awarding compensation.

Now, in view of above, claimants would entitle to receive compensation as follow:
 Heads Amount  Annual Income Rs. 40,000/-
 40% Future Prospective rise Rs. 16,000/-
 Total Rs. 56,000/-
 1/4th personal expenses Rs.14,000/-
 Total Rs.42,000/-

10. Conclusion:
10.1
In view of the aforesaid, claimants are entitled to receive an additional compensation Rs.4,80,000/- with 7.5% interest from the date of claim petition till its realization.
10.2 The claimant no.1 - father of deceased died during pendency of the claim petition, no amount towards filial consortium is granted.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 10.3
The respondent insurance companies shall deposit additional compensation as per its share of liability so fixed by the tribunal within 8 weeks from the date of receipt of the order.

10.4 Once an additional compensation shall be deposited by the respondent insurance company, the same shall be disbursed in favour of the original claimants as per the respective shares so fixed by the tribunal while passing impugned judgment and award.

So far as 25% share of claimant NO.1 is concerned, having so observed earlier that he already died during the pendency of the claim petition, his share of award be equally distributed and disbursed between the claimant Nos. 4 and 5 i.e. daughter and son of deceased.
The tribunal shall pay/disburse entire additional compensation to the claimants in aforesaid proportion by RTGS / NEFT, in accordance with law.
10.5 The impugned award stands modified to the aforesaid extent.
The award may be drawn accordingly.

8.2 Consideration of income of deceased:
8.2.1
The deceased was aged about 30 years old at the time of accident running shop in the city of Surendranagar
. He would having certificate of registration of his shop issued by local self government being Bombay Shops and Establishment Act.
He was also possessing certificate of Meshar and company certifying that deceased had successfully completed the course of VCR Technician and these factors if taking into account and keeping in mind year of accident i.e. 1999, we would not find any exaggeration in claimants claim regarding income of the deceased Rs.40,000/- per annum in their oral evidence submitted through widow of deceased i.e. claimant No.3. 8.2.2
When the claimants themselves contended before the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined tribunal that deceased was used to earn Rs. 40,000/ per year (net income) than now, it would not be appropriate on the part of the ld.
for the claimants to submit and to consider higher income of the deceased i.e. Rs. 7000/ p.m. -
. Moreover, there is neither any accounts of business of the deceased produced on record nor any ITRs of the deceased on record justifying such higher claim and even no person working with the deceased was examined.
Thereby, accepting deceased was used to earn Rs.40,000/- per annum.
The tribunal has not at all awarded any future prospective rise of income of deceased while granting loss of dependency to the claimants.
It is well settled position of law in view of decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra) in a case of self employed also, Court/ tribunal has to consider the future prospective income of the deceased /
victim.
As deceased was aged about 30 years also being self employed at the time of accident, 40%
future prospective income requires to be considered.
So, we are not granting loss of filial consortium to claimant No.1 who NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1049/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined already died.
Even otherwise an amount of filial consortium is the personal claim of an individual which r e q u i r e s t o b e a w a r d e d t o a n i n d i v i d u a l a s p e r s o n c o n c e r n l o s s company/companionship of deceased.
As per Section 306 of Indian Succession Act,
such personal claim would not survive after death of a person in favour of his surviving legal heirs.
He would for about three and half months must have undergone pain and suffering of accidental injuries which he had received due to the accident.
It remained undisputed before the tribunal that cause of death was due to injuries sustained by him, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case of the present case and considering nature of injuries sustained by the claimants, who of-course conscious during the course of treatment, but having intermittently long hospitalization before his death, we are inclined to grant Rs.30,000/- towards pain, shock and suffering instead of Rs.15,000/- granted by the tribunal.
So considering aforesaid medical evidence which remained undisputed before the tribunal, claimants would entitle to receive reasonable attendant charges in absence of any actual payment made to the attendant.
